outcome: No resolution, partial case, or bound has been found since 26 January 2024; the problem (Novikov/Olshanskii's question, listed as Problem 8.52 in the Kourovka Notebook, compared there with Bieri's related Problem 6.3) remains explicitly listed as unsolved in the 21st edition of the Kourovka Notebook (arXiv:1401.0300v40, dated 18 Jan 2026).
summary: This is the Novikov problem (posed by A. Yu. Olshanskii, listed as Problem 8.52 'Do there exist infinite finitely presented periodic groups?' in the Kourovka Notebook, with the related type-(FP)_infinity version as R. Bieri's Problem 6.3, 'Is every periodic group of type (FP)_infinity finite?'). All known infinite periodic groups (Golod, Novikov-Adian free Burnside groups, Grigorchuk group, Gupta-Sidki groups, Tarski monsters) are only finitely generated, not finitely presented, so the question of whether an infinite finitely presented periodic group can exist remains open. I checked the most current authoritative source for open problems in group theory, the Kourovka Notebook's 21st edition (arXiv:1401.0300, version 40, dated 18 January 2026, well inside the window), and confirmed via its HTML rendering that Problem 8.52 is still listed without any solving reference or comment indicating progress; it is simply noted 'compare with 6.3.' I also checked arXiv listings in math.GR for 2024-2026 (searches for 'finitely presented periodic group', 'infinite finitely presented periodic group construction', and related terms), the Groupprops subwiki page on finitely presented periodic groups (last substantively edited 2014, still describing the conjecture as open, consistent with no change), Baumslag's 'Open problems in combinatorial group theory' survey, and general web/MathOverflow searches for any 2024-2026 activity. The only nearby results found were about weakly finitely presented periodic groups (a strictly weaker notion, pre-dating the window) and a 2025 paper on 'dice periodic groups' (arXiv:2504.00838, Petrogradsky) constructing new finitely generated (not finitely presented) infinite periodic groups — a related-but-distinct construction that does not bear on finite presentability, so it is out of scope under the case-vs-variant rule (§3.1) and does not change the status. No AI system was found associated with any activity on this problem in the window; no papers, announcements, or the Kourovka Notebook's own record credit any AI tool with work on this question. This is a well-evidenced 'nothing happened' record.
competing_reading: One could argue the 2025 Petrogradsky 'dice periodic groups' construction (arXiv:2504.00838) is relevant progress, since it is a new construction technique for infinite periodic groups. However, it produces only finitely generated (not finitely presented) periodic groups, which is exactly the gap the Novikov problem is about — these constructions do not touch finite presentability, so under the scope rule this is a related problem (or at most tangential background), not a case of the stated problem, and should not move the status.
what_would_settle_it: A construction of an infinite finitely presented periodic group (resolving it in the negative direction relative to finiteness), a proof that all finitely presented periodic groups are finite, or an explicit comment/reference attached to Problem 8.52 in a future Kourovka Notebook edition indicating a solution or partial result.
